AppEventResult.description: Empty successful results acknowledge completed local acceptance. Field errors preserve the caller's submitted snapshot and do not acknowledge a save.

value.description: Raw form value; routing identity remains separate from stored content.

Contribution.description: A plugin's request to claim a single ExtensionPoint instance.

caps.description: Provider contributions (CI / issue / forge) declare the seam's caps struct here; the host deserializes it into the seam's `XCaps` at load (missing keys ⇒ `false`, least privilege). `Null` for non-providers.

chord.description: `PaletteAction` contributions may ask for a default chord (the user's `[keybinds]` still wins).

oneOf.description: A `PaletteAction` contribution was invoked (`payload.id`).
The active worktree changed (`payload.path`, `payload.branch`).
A session's process exited (`payload.session`, `payload.code`).
A notification was raised (`payload` = the notification).
Anything else: a newer host's event a v0.2 plugin does not know, kept rather than dropped so it can still be logged or ignored by name.

ExtensionPoint.description: The typed slots the host offers for plugins to fill.

oneOf.description: Resident application tab rendered from an [`crate::plugin_app::AppView`] (API 0.4).

Reserved v0.3 vocabulary for a plugin-contributed accordion section in the info panel. The wire shape and cached [`View`] model are stable, but current hosts negotiate this point as unsupported until host-side accordion placement and row activation land.

The plugin IS an issue-tracker backend: the host bridges the issue seam's operations to it as `provider.call` requests (`seam: "issues"`). The contribution's `caps` may carry provider facts; its `label` is the account name shown in the panel.
Reserved vocabulary: a plugin-backed CI provider. Accepted by the wire, negotiated unsupported by the host until CI selection can name plugin providers.
Reserved vocabulary: a plugin-backed forge. Same status as [`ExtensionPoint::CiProvider`].
Reserved vocabulary: a plugin-backed debugger adapter (DAP) provider. Accepted by the wire, negotiated unsupported until the host's debug seam can bridge plugin adapters.

Frame.description: One NDJSON line, either direction. A line with `method` is a message (request when it carries `id`, notification otherwise); a line with `result` or `error` is a response. A bare `{"method": …}` still decodes as a v0.1 message.

oneOf.description: Invoke a host capability by catalog id (`{"cap": "sessions.list", "params": {…}}`), checked against the plugin's scope set exactly as a control-API token would be. A request: carries an `id` and gets a [`RpcResponse`].

id.description: Stable action/row/node identity, never a display label.

PluginManifest.description: The plugin's identity and its full capability/contribution declaration.

PluginMode.description: How the host runs a plugin process.

oneOf.description: Spawn per poll/render, read NDJSON to exit (the calendar `command` source's shape). Stdin is closed.
One long-lived process driven over stdin/stdout for the session.

PluginSpec.description: Everything needed to *run* a plugin: the manifest says what it is, the spec says how to start it. This is the `[[plugins]]` config shape (and a `plugin.toml` in a plugin directory); every field beyond the manifest has a default, so a v0.1 manifest plus `command` is a valid v0.2 spec.

background.description: User permission for declared `background:sync` work while the plugin's app tab is hidden. Effective only for resident plugins that declare the capability; declaring it still requires `trusted_native`.

command.description: argv — never a shell string, so arguments with spaces survive and no shell is involved in launching plugin code.

cwd.description: Working directory; empty = the plugin's own directory (or the host cwd for config-declared plugins).

env.description: Optional child environment. Plain values pass through verbatim; `keyring:`, `env:`, and `file:` references resolve at spawn for config-declared `[[plugins]]` entries through the host secret broker. An unresolved reference refuses the plugin, and references in a directory `plugin.toml` are refused without expansion.

scopes.description: Host-capability scopes this plugin holds for `host.call` — the same lattice as control-API tokens (`read` / `write` / `git` / `merge_add` / `exec` / `admin`), so a plugin is authorised exactly like a paired client. Write, Git, and Exec are independent; Admin implies all of them.

timeout_secs.description: Per-call (one-shot: per-run) wall-clock cap before the process group is killed, clamped to [`MAX_PLUGIN_TIMEOUT_SECS`] seconds.

trusted_native.description: Explicitly opts this plugin into running as unsandboxed native code with the user's full authority. Declared capabilities and scopes are protocol checks, not executable containment.

RpcErrorCode.description: Why a request failed, in a vocabulary both directions share. Provider plugins map these onto the seam's [`ErrorClass`](crate::seam::ErrorClass) (`unsupported` ⇒ the same value a defaulted optional op returns).

params.description: Defaulted so a verb that carries no arguments can be written as a bare `{"method":"..."}` — a plugin author shouldn't have to type `"params":{}`.

RpcResponse.description: A reply to an `id`-bearing [`RpcMessage`], either direction. Exactly one of `result` / `error` is set.

Scope.description:
One capability a control-API token can hold.

`Git` deliberately does **not** imply `Write` (a phone that can commit must not be able to type into a terminal) and vice versa; `Exec` is a third such independent silo (a client that can trigger pre-declared launches need not be able to type into terminals, and vice versa). All three imply `Read`. `Admin` implies everything. `MergeAdd` is deliberately narrower than the usual implication lattice: it does not imply `Read`.

oneOf.description: List sessions/worktrees/leases, snapshots, the event feed.
Send terminal input, resize/split/record/kill sessions, open worktrees, and mutate issues, dispatches and notifications. (There is no browser surface in v1.)
Stage/commit through the GitBackend seam.
Enqueue one registered remote worktree on its owning host. This is a deliberately single-verb grant used by provisioned environments; it cannot stage, commit, list queues, or clear queues.
Launch a pre-declared `[[presets]]` shape into a workspace (`open --preset`). Runs configured commands — its own tier so an `open`/`write` token cannot execute launches, and vice versa.
Pairing management, daemon shutdown.

slot.description: v0.3: an optional theme-slot name the host resolves against its own token vocabulary (`chrome::S` slots). When absent — or naming a slot this host does not know — the span renders with its [`StyleRole`] instead, so an older host ignores it and an older plugin never sends it. Untrusted display data: the host resolves the name; it is never a host action.

rows.description: v0.3: optional multi-row content (rows of spans). Empty means "single line" and the wire bytes are identical to v0.2 (skipped when empty), so an older host ignores it and an older plugin never sends it.

spans.description: The single-line content — the v0.2 compat path an older plugin keeps using. When [`View::rows`] is non-empty it is the effective content and this is the first row (or empty for a pure multi-row view).

x-thegn-extension-support.owner: native automation engine; no plugin adapter
